parse.title: Auditory distortion
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>
An '''auditory distortion''' is the experience of perceived alterations in how audible noises present and structure themselves.<ref name="Carbonaro2013">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Carbonaro, T. M.)), ((Forster, M. J.)), ((Gatch, M. B.)) | journal=Psychopharmacology | title=Discriminative stimulus effects of N,N-diisopropyltryptamine | volume=226 | issue=2 | pages=241–246 | date= March 2013 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00213-012-2891-x | issn=0033-3158 | doi=10.1007/s00213-012-2891-x}}</ref><ref name="Juszczak2013">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Juszczak, G. R.)), ((Swiergiel, A. H.)) | journal=Journal of Psychoactive Drugs | title=Recreational Use of D-Lysergamide from the Seeds of Argyreia Nervosa , Ipomoea Tricolor, Ipomoea Violacea, and Ipomoea Purpurea in Poland | volume=45 | issue=1 | pages=79–93 | date=1 January 2013 | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/02791072.2013.763570 | issn=0279-1072 | doi=10.1080/02791072.2013.763570}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Mehta, U. M.)), ((Naveen Kumar, C.)), ((Venkatasubramanian, G.)), ((Thirthalli, J.)) | journal=Clinical Schizophrenia & Related Psychoses | title=Multimodal Sensory Distortions in Postpartum Exacerbation of Schizophrenia | volume=10 | issue=4 | pages=222–224 | date= January 2017 | url=http://clinicalschizophrenia.org/doi/10.3371/CSRP.MEKU.112013 | issn=1935-1232 | doi=10.3371/CSRP.MEKU.112013}}</ref><ref name="Weinel2016" />

These distortions can manifest in many styles, but commonly take the form of echoes or murmurs which rise in the wake of each sound and are accompanied by fluctuating changes in speed and pitch.<ref name="Weinel2016">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Weinel, J.)) | journal=Contemporary Music Review | title=Entoptic Phenomena in Audio : Categories of Psychedelic Electroacoustic Composition | volume=35 | issue=2 | pages=202–223 | date=3 March 2016 | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/07494467.2016.1221633 | issn=0749-4467 | doi=10.1080/07494467.2016.1221633}}</ref><ref name="Strassman2000">{{cite book | vauthors=((Strassman, R.)) | date= 2001 | title=DMT: the spirit molecule: a doctor’s revolutionary research into the biology of near-death and mystical experiences | publisher=Park Street Press | isbn=9780892819270}}
</ref><ref name="Stanciu2016">{{cite journal | vauthors=((N. Stanciu, C.)), ((M. Penders, T.)) | journal=Current Psychiatry Reviews | title=Hallucinogen Persistent Perception Disorder Induced by New Psychoactive Substituted Phenethylamines; A Review with Illustrative Case | volume=12 | issue=2 | pages=221–223 | date=1 June 2016}}</ref> This can intensify up to the point where sounds are consistently followed by continuous reverberation,<ref name="Espiard2005">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Espiard, M.-L.)), ((Lecardeur, L.)), ((Abadie, P.)), ((Halbecq, I.)), ((Dollfus, S.)) | journal=European Psychiatry | title=Hallucinogen persisting perception disorder after psilocybin consumption: a case study | volume=20 | issue=5–6 | pages=458–460 | date= August 2005 | url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S092493380024145X/type/journal_article | issn=0924-9338 | doi=10.1016/j.eurpsy.2005.04.008}}</ref> often rendering the original sound completely unrecognizable. However, it often quickly resets to base level and starts over if the source of noise is stopped or changed.

The experience of this effect can be broken down into three distinct levels of intensity. These are described and documented below:

#'''Mild''' - At the lowest level of intensity, auditory distortions consist of subtle and spontaneous reverberation,<ref name="Weinel2016" /><ref name="Strassman2000" /><ref name="Espiard2005" /> echo effects,<ref name="Weinel2016" /><ref name="Stanciu2016" /> and changes in pitch<ref name="Weinel2016" /><ref name="Strassman2000" /><ref name="Stanciu2016" /><ref name="Shulgin1997">{{cite book | vauthors=((Shulgin, A.)), ((Shulgin, A.)) | date= 1997 | title=TIHKAL: The Continuation | publisher=Transform Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Strassman, R. J.)), ((Qualls, C. R.)), ((Berg, L. M.)) | journal=Biological Psychiatry | title=Differential tolerance to biological and subjective effects of four closely spaced doses of N,N-dimethyltryptamine in humans | volume=39 | issue=9 | pages=784–795 | date= May 1996 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0006322395002006 | issn=00063223 | doi=10.1016/0006-3223(95)00200-6}}</ref> of noises within the external environment. They are fleeting, low in intensity, and easy to ignore.
#'''Distinct''' - At this level, auditory distortions consist of distinctly noticeable, spontaneous echo effects and changes in pitch attributed to noises within the external environment. They are long and drawn out and loud enough to become difficult to ignore.
#'''All-encompassing''' - At the highest level, auditory distortions become constant and impossible to ignore. The complexity of the resulting alterations quickly renders the original sound as unintelligible.<ref name="Juszczak2013" />

Auditory distortions are often accompanied by other coinciding effects such as [[auditory hallucinations]],<ref name="Stanciu2016" /><ref name="Shulgin1997" /><ref name="Carbonaro2013" /> [[Auditory acuity suppression|auditory acuity suppression]], and [[Auditory acuity enhancement|auditory acuity enhancement]].<ref name="Juszczak2013" /><ref name="Weinel2016" /> They are most commonly induced under the influence of [[dosage#common|moderate]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[psychedelic]] compounds,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Meatherall, R.)), ((Sharma, P.)) | journal=Journal of Analytical Toxicology | title=Foxy, a Designer Tryptamine Hallucinogen* | volume=27 | issue=5 | pages=313–317 | date=1 July 2003 | url=http://academic.oup.com/jat/article/27/5/313/752418/Foxy-a-Designer-Tryptamine-Hallucinogen | issn=1945-2403 | doi=10.1093/jat/27.5.313}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Mowry, M.)), ((Mosher, M.)), ((Briner, W.)) | journal=Journal of Psychoactive Drugs | title=Acute Physiologic and Chronic Histologic Changes in Rats and Mice Exposed to the Unique Hallucinogen Salvinorin A | volume=35 | issue=3 | pages=379–382 | date= September 2003 | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/02791072.2003.10400021 | issn=0279-1072 | doi=10.1080/02791072.2003.10400021}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Leake, C. D.)) | journal=JAMA: The Journal of the American Medical Association | title=Hallucinogenic Drug Reaction—MDA | volume=219 | issue=8 | pages=1069 | date=21 February 1972 | url=http://jama.jamanetwork.com/article.aspx?doi=10.1001/jama.1972.03190340073029 | issn=0098-7484 | doi=10.1001/jama.1972.03190340073029}}</ref> such as [[LSD]], [[5-MeO-DiPT]], and [[DMT]]. However, they can also occur less commonly under the influence of [[dissociatives]] such as [[ketamine]],<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Hillhouse, T. M.)), ((Porter, J. H.)), ((Negus, S. S.)) | journal=Psychopharmacology | title=Reply to: Rapid antidepressant effects and abuse liability of ketamine | volume=231 | issue=9 | pages=2043–2044 | date=1 May 2014 | url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00213-014-3544-z | issn=1432-2072 | doi=10.1007/s00213-014-3544-z}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Oye, I.)), ((Paulsen, O.)), ((Maurset, A.)) | journal=The Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics | title=Effects of ketamine on sensory perception: evidence for a role of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors | volume=260 | issue=3 | pages=1209–1213 | date= March 1992 | issn=0022-3565}}</ref> [[PCP]], and [[nitrous]].<ref name="Weinel2016" /><ref name="Strassman2000" />
